primitives.name: Stance Synchronization
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ability of an offensive line man to start sharply and powerfully from a strong stance to a hard charge, which is properly followed up by his feet with short steps, marks the critical point of the rushing attack.
primitives.assumptions: Player stance is modeled as a rigid body with fixed base of support; initial velocity v_0 is zero; acceleration a is constant during charge.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t_s > 0.1 seconds or d_f < 0.5 meters, charge initiation fails.

layer2.mapping: Charge initiation trajectory maps to GSE state transition from stance to motion; GSI computes posterior probability of successful charge given stance parameters.
layer2.telemetry: Footstep timing variance, stance angle deviation, and acceleration profile.

primitives.name: Signal Coordination
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the team has a starting signal, the charge and the signal should be practiced constantly for the various plays, against a dummiy defense.
primitives.assumptions: Signal and charge are synchronized with minimal temporal jitter; ΔT = T_charge - T_signal is bounded.

layer2.mapping: Signal-to-charge timing is isomorphic to GSI temporal alignment model; GSE simulates multi-agent timing convergence.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal jitter between signal and charge initiation across drills.

primitives.name: Footstep Kinematics
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ability of an offensive line man to start sharply and powerfully from a strong stance to a hard charge, which is properly followed up by his feet with short steps, marks the critical point of the rushing attack.
primitives.assumptions: Each step is modeled as a discrete impulse; v_step = s_step / t_step; cumulative step distance defines forward progress.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When v_step < 1.5 m/s or s_step < 0.3 meters per step, charge efficiency degrades.

layer2.mapping: Footstep kinematics map to GSE motion planning kernel; GSI evaluates step consistency via variance in stride metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Stride length, step frequency, and velocity consistency across repeated drills.
